Floods hit southern region

Heavy rain has flooded dozens of towns and villages across the southern region, forcing thousands of residents to leave their homes overnight, officials said on Tuesday.

The national weather service said more than 200 millimetres of rain fell in 24 hours, the highest total recorded in the area since measurements began in the 1950s.

Emergency shelters have been opened in schools and sports halls, and the army has been asked to help with evacuations in the worst-affected districts.

Related: how to prepare for flooding in your area.

Regional governor Maria Santos told reporters that the immediate priority was to reach people cut off by rising water, and that damage assessments would begin once levels fall.
